name: Garcia Park Dispersed Camping Area - Carson National Forest (FR 437)

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Camino Real Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted on general national forest lands along Forest Road 437 (Garcia Park road corridor). Must park within one vehicle length of established pullouts.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6 inches deep in high mountain soil, at least 200 feet from streams and springs. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace. Black bears active in Sangre de Cristo Mountains: bear canister or hard-sided vehicle food storage mandatory.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established rock fire rings only. Extinguish cold to touch with water.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Stage 1 and Stage 2 fire restrictions common in early summer (May-July) before monsoon season.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved dirt and gravel mountain forest road (FR 437 / FR 76)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Winding mountain dirt road with steep grades, exposed rocks, ruts, and mud holes after rain.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: High clearance car or 4x4 required (Normal 2WD low clearance cars not recommended for upper Garcia Park meadow roads)

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 2-3 bars 4G LTE (10-25 Mbps download on high meadow points)
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate (Sangre de Cristo Mountain peaks surround meadow basin)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: May thaw: cool (45-60°F), high snowmelt mud season, snow lingering on FR 437 until late May.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Ideal high alpine summer (70-78°F daytime, 40-45°F nights), July-August afternoon monsoon thunderstorms.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Golden quaking aspen leaf foliage in September (55-68°F daytime, freezing 20-30°F nights), dry roads.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Severe sub-zero mountain winter (10-30°F), heavy snowpack, FR 437 impassable to wheeled vehicles.

dangers_and_hazards: Black Bears active in Carson NF - bear-proof food storage required
Severe afternoon lightning storms on open meadows during monsoon season

common_human_made_sounds: Occasional passing 4x4 or OHV vehicle on FR 437
Cattle lowing in seasonal grazing meadow

human_demographics_and_culture: Taos artists, high-elevation digital nomads, mountain bikers, autumn leaf peepers, and elk hunters.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Taos Pueblo indigenous traditions revere the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and high alpine meadows as sacred emergence lands of spiritual ancestors.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Profound high-altitude mountain clarity, crisp pine-aspen air ionization, inspiring Sangre de Cristo vistas.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding alpine meadow trail through aspen groves with mountain vistas

public_reviews_summary: High-altitude summer boondocking paradise near Taos. Spectacular aspen groves, cool summer temps, and dependable cell service in open meadow spots.
other_data: Bortle Class 2 night sky. High clearance vehicle mandatory.

name: Gila National Forest / Gila Wilderness Dispersed Camping

management_agency.name: US Forest Service - Gila National Forest (Wilderness Ranger District)

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - Gila National Forest Primitive Dispersed Land (zero fee)
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping along Forest Road 150 (North Wall) and Gila River access pullouts. Leave No Trace.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Dig cat-hole 6-8 inches deep in soil 200 feet from Gila River and natural springs. Pack out hygiene products.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Abundant dead and down pine and oak firewood gathering permitted.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established stone rings. Douse thoroughly with water before leaving.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Spring dry windy season fire restrictions common May-June.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved NM 15 to unpaved Forest Road gravel/dirt
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Winding mountain pavement, rough gravel dirt roads.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: High clearance recommended for Forest Road 150; standard 2WD can reach pavement pullouts near Gila Cliff Dwellings.

nomad_connectivity_rating.overall_rating: Low to Moderate / Mountain Ridge Dependent
nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 1-2 bars 4G LTE near high highway passes; SOS in deep canyons
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: High (Deep volcanic canyon walls block signals)

amenities: Nearby Natural Thermal Hot Springs (Lightfeather / Jordan Hot Springs access)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 50-70°F, windy afternoon high mountain breeze, river snowmelt runoff.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: 75-88°F, monsoon rain showers in July/August bringing lush green growth.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: 55-72°F, sunny crisp days, ideal backpacking weather.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: 25-48°F, freezing night temps, dusting of snow in high wilderness peaks.

dangers_and_hazards: Summer afternoon monsoon flash floods in canyon drainages
Black bears and mountain lions (store food securely)

acoustic_environment.quietness_rating: 10/10 - Absolute wilderness canyon silence and river breeze

human_demographics_and_culture: Chiricahua Apache homeland, Aldo Leopold conservation heritage, desert mountain nomads.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: First Wilderness area in the world designated by Aldo Leopold in 1924. Rich Mogollon Native American archaeological history.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Profound high desert wilderness silence, natural hot spring healing energy.

nearby_hiking_trails.trail_name: Middle Fork Gila River Trail to Jordan Hot Springs
nearby_hiking_trails.features: Multiple river crossings, towering volcanic canyon walls, thermal soak pools

public_reviews_summary: World-class wilderness camping in New Mexico's Gila National Forest. Natural hot springs, majestic ponderosa forests, and complete off-grid solitude.
other_data: Free Gila National Forest dispersed land. Bring water filter and satellite communicator.
